newsitem.title: JAPAN: Denso considers entering LCD business.
newsitem.headline: Denso considers entering LCD business.

text.p: Japanese electronic parts maker Denso Corp said on Tuesday that it is considering entering the liquid crystal display (LCD) business.
A Denso spokesman, however, said that the company has not made a final decision yet.

Nevertheless, the spokesman said that the type of LCDs that the company is considering producing can respond about 1,000 times faster than conventional thin-film transistor LCDs, making the device suitable for video.
The company will probably procure basic materials for production of LCDs from Showa Shell Sekiyu KK, he said.

The Nihon Keizai Shimbun business daily reported on Tuesday that the Toyota Motor Corp affiliate will start making the device in mid-1998 and further invest about 40 billion yen to build an LCD factory by 2000.
The LCDs are expected to be used in Toyota's car-navigation systems as well as be supplied to personal computer makers.
The company aims for 50-60 billion yen in sales in 2000/01 from the flat-panel business, the paper said.
